text:
Maya: quick check — following up on the slimline adapter vs ownership zones debate from the RFC. thoughts?

chris: tl;dr: adapter keeps queueing simple but leaks latency control; ownership gives headroom but complicates placement.

danny: can you scope the failure modes? e.g., adapter hit cold-kv cache and queue stalls vs owner eject path

maya: good point. I sketched two failure cases:
- adapter overload: single adapter tries to pack variable-length seqs -> long tails
- owner imbalance: tenant pinned to slab with hot spikes -> local starvation

olivia: another axis: observability. adapters can emit uniform metrics; ownership requires per-slab telemetry + eviction signals.

chris: perf numbers from the alpha run:
```
adapter baseline p95: 40ms
adapter heavy: p95 220ms
owner baseline p95: 35ms
owner heavy (rebalance ongoing): p95 180ms
```

chris: both suffer on long tokens; owner allows faster global redispatch but needs lease heartbeats.

maya: also cost: owner needs more inter-node network during rebalances. adapter mostly local but stalls waste GPU cycles.

danny: operationally, owner needs stronger invariants: "slot ownership lease" and a reassign backoff. adapter needs admission backpressure + per-tenant caps.

olivia: propose a hybrid: short requests served by adapters (fastpath); long/risky ones go through ownership lanes. simple policy: token_len > 128 -> ownership. Thoughts?

chris: I like hybrid. Add a TTL on ownership leases (e.g., 1s) and a soft-failover: if owner not responding, fall back to adapter with degraded qos.

maya: suggested rollout plan:
1) feature-flag hybrid in staging (metrics: p95, token-cost, evictions/sec)
2) enable token_len routing for 10% of traffic
3) monitor and iterate on lease TTL and backoff

infra-bot: deploy queued: staging/hybrid-adapter-owner v0.4 scheduled in 30m :rocket:

danny: can someone add a K-V cache warmup probe? adapter cold path is killer.

olivia: I'll add a telemetry PR with warmup histograms and a lease-acquisition trace span.

chris: one last note — make sure the admission API surface has an explicit `handback()` so owners can return partially-filled batches to adapter pools.

maya: agreed. I'll open a short RFC addendum with the hybrid policy, TTL defaults, and the handback API. thanks all :thumbsup:
